newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call money up on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call money up on tight supply.

text.p: Dutch money market rates were unchanged in thin trading except for overnight guilders which rose to 2.75 percent from 2.68 percent bid on a tight allocation of a new special advances loan from the Dutch central bank.

The allocation was 2.11 billion guilders for a seven-day pact which took effect today. Meanwhile the Dutch state had difficulty selling its new Treasury Certificates (DTCs) which were priced at 2.78 percent, three basis points above Monday's introduction price but not enough to attract many investors.
The DTCs run from October 21 to maturity on January 2, February 28 and March 27. They replace expiring DTCs.
In the interbank market, one- to three-month deposits traded on a par at 2.75/82 percent, levels at which they have been pegged for several weeks now.
"The prices are unchanged and so is the mood on the trading floor, unaltered and bad," one trader said with a grim smile.
The guilder weakened slightly to around 112.24 per 100 marks, although the discount of Dutch bonds and deposits to German equivalents remained static.
